cards.body:
## Summary
lab-ui.ts is a 1,166-line class doing eight jobs, its mode is a hidden state machine across six fields, and its replay ring re-implements (forward-only, at a hard-coded 60 Hz) the transport BoutReader already has. Extract three pure modules - a LabMode reducer, a ReplayTransport shared with BoutReader, and a forecast-view formatter - plus a core coupled-tuning helper beside validateTuning, leaving lab-ui.ts a thin canvas layer.

## Description
The Lab is the owner's tuning bench, yet none of its behaviour is tested: arena-entry.ts is its only importer. Every new Lab capability (tiger C replay takeover, a compare mode, feel capsules) has to be wired into the same class and its boolean gates, and the host peeks at replayState in four places. The reducer makes modes explicit (live, replay, setup, builds, tuning, number, import), so hotkey gating and pause restoration are data, not scattered ifs. The transport gives the Lab step-back for free and removes the per-frame full-state clone. The forecast formatter moves 57 lines of string/tint logic out of the draw path into a testable function. The tuning coupling rule moves next to the validation that already enforces it.

## Flow
- Add coupleTuningField to core tuning.ts with a lab.test.ts case; lab-ui setTuning calls it.
- Add replay-transport.ts (frames or seek callback, position, playing, carry, advance, step, seek); BoutReader delegates to it; Lab replay uses it over labReplay(lab).
- Add lab-mode.ts reducer (mode, key -> action | notice | unhandled) and lab-forecast-view.ts (ForecastView -> rows/lines/tints).
- lab-ui.ts draws from these; keeps replayState getter for arena-entry.ts.

## Expected impact
lab-ui.ts shrinks by ~300 lines; Lab logic goes from 0 to ~25 unit tests; the Lab replay gains step-back and loses a per-frame structuredClone of the full state; tiger C and slot B become additive instead of invasive.

## Evaluation
Claim: the Lab's mode, transport and forecast-view logic become pure, tested modules with no behaviour or simulation change.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (modules do not exist; no test imports Lab UI logic)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - vitest for the three new test files plus unchanged bout-reader.test.ts, then npm run gate and npm run build:game; replay goldens and parity vectors untouched.
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.title: Pin a baseline: Lab forecast compares against your pinned tuning + builds
shared_surfaces: packages/core/src/arena/forecast.ts (consumed: censusForecast, duelForecast, forecastDeltas; not edited)
acceptance: case 1: runForecast with no baseline -> result identical to today (existing forecast.test.ts cases pass unchanged, sameAsCurrent semantics kept)
case 2: request whose baseline equals the candidate (same tuning and lab) -> sameAsCurrent true, candidate deep-equals current, and a repeat plan has total 0
case 3: baseline tuning absorbWindowS 0.25 pinned, candidate factory tuning -> every wave's perfectRateDelta equals the negation of the factory-baseline/0.25-candidate run

case 4: baseline lab = defaultLabConfig, candidate lab = an Air build (withSchool player air) -> result.current.duel equals drain(duelForecast(makeTuning(), default plan)) and duelDelta.winRate = candidate.winRate - current.winRate

case 7: lab-compare pin(tuning, draft, 'Brawler v2') -> label 'vs pinned Brawler v2'; unpin -> 'vs Current'; pinning a draft that fails validateLabConfig -> refused with the validator's reason, pin unchanged

cards.body:
## Summary
The Lab forecast can only ever tell the owner how a change compares to the factory preset. Tuning is iterative: the question is 'is this better than what I had five minutes ago', and the builds page cannot answer 'is this Air build better than the last one' at all. Add a pinned baseline - tuning plus both sides' builds, named - that the forecast compares against, with the delta shown on both the tuning panel and the builds page.

## Description
ForecastRequest gains an optional baseline {tuning, lab}. ForecastRunner memoises baseline waves by (tuning key, difficulty) and baseline duels by (tuning, lab) key, as it already does for Current, so a pinned baseline is computed once and every candidate after it costs only its own fights. ForecastClient folds the baseline into its key. A small pure module lab-compare.ts holds the pin (name, tuning, lab), produces the panel label and the duel delta, and refuses an unplayable pin. lab-ui.ts adds 'Pin as baseline' / 'Unpin' on the tuning and builds pages and renders 'vs pinned <name>' and signed duel deltas. No band, sample size or balance value changes; the census path and its hashes are untouched when no baseline is pinned.

## Flow
- Owner tunes or picks builds, presses Pin (name defaults to the tuning name or the archetype plan).
- Further edits forecast against the pin: per-wave median/win/perfect deltas and duel win %/TTK deltas.
- Unpin returns to 'vs Current'.

## Expected impact
Turns a five-step manual compare (export JSON, note seed and setup, re-import, re-run, read two numbers) into one press; gives the builds page its first comparative read, which is the WP4 census target's day-to-day instrument.

## Evaluation
Claim: the Lab forecast compares against a pinned tuning + builds baseline, with no change when nothing is pinned.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no baseline field, no lab-compare module)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - vitest forecast.test.ts (existing cases unchanged) + lab-compare.test.ts, then npm run gate and npm run build:game.
Result: better
Gate: direction
